title: Monsters and Their Ways

sections.heading: Every creature fights its own way
paragraphs: Look at a creature (O) to see what it shows of its ways. The more you know of its kind, the more you are told: what it can do, and what to do about it.

sections.heading: When they break
paragraphs: Badly hurt, a creature may break, the way its nature says. The mindless dead, constructs, oozes and plants never do. A beast bolts and gives up the fight. A goblin or a bandit runs for its friends and comes back with them: kill the runner first. A giant or a demon falls back, fighting as it goes. Caught with no friend and nowhere to go, a bandit may throw down his weapon and his purse and beg; you may spare him or not. Cornered, any of them turns at bay and fights harder.

sections.heading: Held fast
rows: Coils
A python, a naga or a sea serpent that wraps round you squeezes every turn, and you cannot walk away. One hard blow on it breaks the coils; a step away is a struggle that may twist you free.
Swallowed
A gelatinous cube or a taniwha can take you inside it. Its gut eats at you, but nothing else can reach you there, and your spells reach only it. Cut your way out with one hard blow.
Dragged under
A kelpie or Grendel's mother drags you toward the water and pulls you under at its edge. Strike hard to tear free, and keep away from the water.
Loosed
The Galdr of Loosing and the Coif of Beowulf keep any grip off you; the Psylli's charm keeps off a serpent's. No hold lasts more than a few turns, and after one you are steady for a moment.

sections.heading: Casters
rows: Wards
A hurt shaman or lich chants a ward up about himself, and your blows land weak until it fades. Spells, wands and thrown flasks pass it.
Curses
A curse is drawn up for a turn first: strike the caster while he chants and it breaks. Wax in your ears stops a spoken one, a mirror an evil eye.
Other tricks
A lich can tear a spell off you, a dark elf can put out your light, a hag can step away from your blade. A silenced caster can do none of it.

sections.heading: Auras
rows: Dread
To see a dullahan, a death knight or an old dragon close is dread: once a fight your will must hold, and then it cannot shake you again.
Heat and cold
A fire or frost elemental, a fire or frost giant, burns or numbs you every turn you stand beside it. Fight it from a little way off, or ward off its fire or cold.
Reek
A ghast's or a mapinguari's reek can turn your stomach, until you once master it.

sections.heading: Home ground and what they carry
rows: Home ground
A draugr in its mound, a troll in its lair, a dragon on its hoard will not follow you far from its ground, and on it it never runs. Hurt, leave its ground, rest and come back.
What they carry
A bandit captain or an orc chief may carry a potion he drinks when badly hurt, or a pot of fire oil he throws from a few paces. Kill him fast and what he did not use is yours.
Lurkers
A spider or a wight lying in wait drops on you with a surprise blow, unless you spot it first. A chest you know for a mimic cannot surprise you.
The Leprechaun
He keeps out of reach and darts in when you turn your back. Corner him and he offers his purse for his freedom: take it, or fight him for all he carries.

sections.heading: Breath, drain and rot
rows: Breath
A dragon, a drake or a winter wolf that has breathed must draw breath again for a few turns. Meanwhile it fights with tooth and claw, and a dragon in its full fury: claw and bite at once.
Life drained
A wight's or a vampire's touch lowers your greatest health. Half comes back with a night's sleep on the next floor down; a physician or a prayer at a chain of four gives back the rest.
Disease
A plague bite or a mummy's touch lingers: while you are diseased, rest does not mend you and potions, spells, prayers and meals heal half. Cure it with a potion, a prayer or a physician.

sections.heading: Light and dark
rows: Light-shy
Trolls, dark elves, shadows and kobolds hate a bright light: in its glow they strike worse, and a troll's wounds will not close. The Light spell's glare is the brightest.
Snuffed
A wave, a gust or a shadow's touch can put out the light in your hand; a soaked wick will not light again at once. A light that never burns out is never snuffed.
Hiders
An imp or a boggart strikes, then hides out of sight until you find it. Some hide in the dark, unseen, unless you carry a light.
Back to the web
A hurt spider that gets out of your sight goes back into hiding to drop on you again. Finish it, or bring a light.

sections.heading: Shouts, chants and bursts
rows: Lookouts
A goblin, a kobold or a raven that sees you raises the alarm, and its kind come running. Kill it first, or never be seen.
Healers
A priest mends a badly hurt friend, then must rest his voice. Kill him first.
Summoners
A necromancer chants for a turn before his dead come. Strike him while he chants and the chant breaks.
Bursting
A fire beetle or a plague zombie that swells or glows is about to burst. Step back, or finish it from afar.
Shoves
A giant's or an ogre's blow can throw you back a step, and a clever giant throws you into what hurts. Keep your back to a wall.

sections.heading: How the clever ones fight
rows: Thinking foes

Goblins, bandits, orcs, hobgoblins, the dark elves and the Fair Folk think about their turn. Beasts, vermin and the mindless dead do not. Observe one, or read its kind in the Bestiary, to learn how it thinks.
Corridors
A clever band will not follow you into a narrow way one at a time. They wait out of sight, come round another way, or shoot down it. They come in the end, but do not count on the corridor alone.
Captains
While a band's leader lives and can shout, his guards stand in front of him and the rest charge when you are hurt. Kill or silence him and the orders stop.
Feints
Drilled soldiers may break and run to draw you out of a corridor, with the rest waiting beside the way out. A foe who runs too neatly is a trap.
The weak one
A cunning foe goes for whoever is bleeding. Call a badly hurt pet back to its Soul Sphere.
The dark edge
Dark elves and shadows keep to the edge of your light and strike from the dark. A brighter light leaves them nowhere to hide.
Archers
An archer steps aside for a clear shot past its friends and keeps its distance. Each missile reaches as far as its weapon: a sling less than a longbow.
Your tricks
What a clever side sees you do on a floor, it learns: fight from corridors twice and they stay in their room. Change your ways, or leave no one to tell.
